Subject: Request: pilot uptime band / credits for HelixGen POC

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team was impressed with the latency profile and the routing controls. We're in the final stages of our procurement review for the Q4 pilot. One hold-up from our internal ops team: the uptime target in the standard SLA (99.9%) is tighter than we can reasonably guarantee for our initial integration window. Specifically we're asking if Redwood can: 

- Temporarily lower the uptime SLO for the first 90 days of the pilot to 99.0% (to reflect our expected orchestration instability while we tune caching), and
- Limit the service credit exposure to a fixed cap (we'd like to propose 30 days equivalent revenue) rather than the open-ended rolling credits in the standard term.

As part of the ask, we're also seeking a one-time onboarding concession to offset integration costs (initial ask: 15% credit on the first month). If Redwood can agree to the pilot carveout plus the onboarding concession, we can sign and start next week.

I know this is non-standard — please let me know what you need from procurement/legal to make a decision.

Best,
Daniel
Director of Platform Operations
HelixGen

Team — forwarding HelixGen's request. Quick summary and ask:

What HelixGen asks for:
- Temporary SLO: 99.0% for first 90 days of pilot
- Credit cap: 30 days equivalent revenue
- One-time onboarding concession: 15% credit on month one

My recommended position to limit risk and unblock the pilot quickly:
- Approve 99.0% for 90 days ONLY, with telemetry gating and a rollback trigger we define (see slide 3 in the SLA_summary).
- Cap credits at 20 days revenue instead of 30.
- Approve a one-time onboarding credit but capped at 10% (commercial concession), or a 15% credit conditioned on a 6-month committed contract at a set MRR.

Why: HelixGen is early stage but we see upside to a quick POC -> pilot conversion. If we push too hard on credits they will walk; if we push too much on discount we set a precedent. I'm asking for an exec authorization to grant the temporary SLO carveout and to set the onboarding credit ceiling.

Please reply with the exact approval language we can send back to the customer (I will not send anything externally until we have explicit sign-off).

Thanks — Priya

Priya — quick thoughts from Deal Desk:

1) Risk/revenue: estimated ARR if pilot converts = $410k ARR; pilot is valued at ~ $18k MRR for month one.
2) Credit exposure: 30-day cap is a material liability for us; 20 days is better but still on the higher side. Recommend a 20 day cap only if we can require an early termination fee outside the credit bucket and have visibility (telemetry) to close the loop.
3) Discount: agree with a 10% onboarding credit unconditional. If customer wants 15%, make it conditional on a 6-month minimum commitment and an accelerated payment schedule.

If Marissa can sign the above (approve temporary 99.0% for 90 days with telemetry gating, 20-day credit cap, and 10% onboarding credit — or 15% with 6-month commit) this unblocks. Also recommend adding a short clause that limits further precedent: "This temporary SLO modification applies only to the initial pilot and may not be referenced in future contracts without prior Commercial approval."

I can turn this into explicit approval language; need Marissa's OK.

—Jonas

Ok — I approve a constrained concession with the following explicit terms (this is executive-level sign-off; send these back to the customer exactly as written below):

Executive approval: Redwood Inference will agree to the following temporary, pilot-only modifications to the standard SLA for HelixGen's initial pilot:

1) Temporary SLO: Uptime SLO of 99.0% for a single, contiguous 90-day pilot window beginning on the Go-Live date. This modification is pilot-only and expires automatically after 90 days.
2) Service credit cap: Service credit exposure is capped at 20 days of invoice-equivalent revenue for the pilot period.
3) Onboarding concession: A one-time onboarding credit of 10% applied to the first month invoice. A 15% onboarding credit may be permitted only if HelixGen signs a minimum 6-month committed contract prior to Go-Live.
4) Telemetry & rollback: The carveout is conditional upon Redwood having access to the pilot telemetry and a weekly sync cadence; a defined rollback trigger will revert the SLO to standard terms if production instability is attributable to HelixGen's environment.
5) Precedent clause: This modification is expressly non-precedential and may not be used as a reference in future contract negotiations without Commercial & Executive approval.

Legal & Finance must review the exact DocuSign and SOW redline, but commercial approval is granted. Priya — please send the approved language back to Daniel and procurement as part of a revised SOW/DocuSign packet. CC Legal (legal@redwood.ai) and Finance.

Marissa Cole
VP, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference
